title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Encore includes deleted Doomsday scene
body_md:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is returning to theaters with additional footage, including a scene originally removed from Avengers: Doomsday. According to a report published on November 26, 2026, the extended theatrical edition is scheduled to arrive on December 4. The inclusion of material from the upcoming Avengers movie gives Marvel audiences another reason to revisit the summer release before the next major crossover.

The coverage cites a New York Times report examining the commercial prospects of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three. According to that account, the Spider-Man rerelease will feature a bonus scene at the end of the movie that was previously cut from Doomsday. The precise contents have not been disclosed, and the footage is described primarily as promotional material for the forthcoming Avengers installment.

The extended edition, marketed as an encore presentation, will also restore Rosario Dawson's appearance as Claire Temple. The character is familiar to viewers of Marvel's television productions, making her restored appearance another point of interest for longtime audiences. The available report does not establish the exact running time of the additional material or explain how every restored scene fits into the revised film.

**Spoiler warning for the original film's ending:** The original post-credits sequence features Ned's tracking technology indicating that Spider-Man is no longer on Earth. The sequence prompted competing interpretations among viewers. Some connected it to Battleworld and the events anticipated in Avengers: Secret Wars, while others suggested that alternate versions of Spider-Man could become involved through the multiverse. These interpretations remain theories rather than officially confirmed plot developments.

The new footage could potentially provide additional context, but its status as a deleted Doomsday scene is an important qualification. Its appearance in the encore edition would not, by itself, confirm Tom Holland's involvement in the final Avengers movie. Nor would it establish that his role was removed from the completed production.

There is also a commercial dimension to the rerelease. According to the report, Brand New Day is approaching the billion-dollar threshold at the domestic box office. Additional screenings and the promise of previously unseen material could help Sony attract returning viewers, although crossing that milestone depends on actual ticket sales.

Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled for December 18, two weeks after the Spider-Man encore arrives. That timing makes the extended edition a promotional bridge between the two releases. Whether the bonus scene provides meaningful narrative answers or simply promotes the upcoming crossover will remain uncertain until audiences see it.
excerpt: The December 4 rerelease will feature restored footage and a deleted Avengers scene.
